{"number":2,"title":"Transparent rounded corners carry a dark ring","body":"## What happens today

round_corner with the transparent flag set, written out as PNG or WebP, draws a thin dark outline along every curved corner. The pixels on the curve stay fully opaque and have their colors scaled toward black. Over any page background the corner looks as if it were traced with a dark pencil. The opaque form of the filter, without the transparent flag, blends its edge cleanly into the fill color.

## What should happen

The curve is smoothed through the alpha channel. Pixels on the edge keep their original color and become partly transparent, so the picture fades into whatever is behind it with no outline. Output formats without alpha, such as JPEG, should still show the fill color in the corners.

## How to see it

Start the image server and open this path in the browser:

/unsafe/300x200/filters:round_corner(60,255,255,255,1):format(png)/example.jpg

Zoom into any corner of the picture. Today a dark ring follows the arc where the picture meets the background. After the fix the arc fades into the background with no ring. The same path with format(webp) in place of format(png) shows the same ring. The image file is example.jpg.

## Where it came from

This is a real bug, reported on the thumbor project as thumbor/thumbor#1687 (https://github.com/thumbor/thumbor/issues/1687). from thumbor.ext.filters import _round_corner
from thumbor.filters import BaseFilter, filter_method


class Filter(BaseFilter):
    @filter_method(
        r"[\d]+(?:\|[\d]+)?",
        BaseFilter.PositiveNumber,
        BaseFilter.PositiveNumber,
        BaseFilter.PositiveNumber,
        BaseFilter.Boolean,
    )
    async def round_corner(
        self, radius, red, green, blue, transparent=False
    ):  # pylint: disable=too-many-positional-arguments
        width, height = self.engine.size
        radius_parts = radius.split("|")
        a_radius = int(radius_parts[0])
        b_radius = int(radius_parts[1]) if len(radius_parts) > 1 else a_radius

        if transparent:
            self.engine.enable_alpha()

        mode, data = self.engine.image_data_as_rgb()
        imgdata = _round_corner.apply(
            1,
            mode,
            a_radius,
            b_radius,
            red,
            green,
            blue,
            width,
            height,
            data,
            transparent,
        )
        self.engine.set_image_data(imgdata)

from tornado.testing import gen_test

from tests.base import FilterTestCase


class RoundCornerTransparentEdgeTestCase(FilterTestCase):
    @gen_test
    async def test_transparent_corner_edge_pixels_are_partly_transparent(
        self,
    ):
        radius = 50
        image = await self.get_filtered(
            "source.jpg",
            "thumbor.filters.round_corner",
            f"round_corner({radius},255,0,0,1)",
            mode="RGBA",
        )

        # The top-left corner box holds the arc. Edge pixels on the arc
        # must fade through alpha, so some of them must be partly
        # transparent (0 < alpha < 255). Today they stay at alpha 255.
        pixels = image.load()
        partial = [
            pixels[x, y][3]
            for x in range(radius)
            for y in range(radius)
            if 0 < pixels[x, y][3] < 255
        ]

        assert len(partial) > 0, (
            "no partly transparent pixels on the corner arc; "
            "edge pixels are fully opaque"
        )
